prompts.cycle:
Create a premium original art-directed SaaS website concept for DrawPacket. Use case ui-mockup. One independent direction named "Cycle Study". Target 1440 × 1600, a desktop marketing page showing its first two chapters and a short design/motion strip at bottom. No browser bezel. Research basis: general contractor project accountants work in a MONTHLY draw review cycle; documents arrive at different times; accountability and dated next action matter. The site should feel deliberately designed by an exceptional independent digital studio, not a templated SaaS page. Do not reuse folders, manila, redline marks, document galleries, engineering registers or stamps. No stock imagery or floating app-card hero.

Visual idea: a beautifully typeset editorial monthly calendar transforms into a review timeline. Bone-free cool chalk #F5F5F1, oxblood #642A37, muted lilac #DFDBE8, ink #252225. Use expressive narrow editorial sans for headlines and neutral readable sans for controls, tabular numbers. Huge negative space, delicate oxblood rules, asymmetric composition, large but controlled type. No gradients. Orange/amber only for labelled holds. Oxblood primary buttons. Pale lilac accent is structural calendar region, not decorative glowing field.

Composition: top quiet DrawPacket bespoke date-tab logo, "Offerings", "How it works", "Controls", "Explore demo". Visible "RESEARCH-STAGE CONCEPT". Left 45% first viewport has massive but elegant typographic headline exactly "Bring the month\ninto focus." supporting copy "A concept for reviewing one construction draw, its evidence and the decisions still open." Two buttons "Explore synthetic demo" and "Discuss a pilot". Small footer at left "One project. One monthly cycle."
Right55% hero: a large editorial FIVE DAY calendar timeline designed as the WEBSITE'S underlying surface, no rounded dashboard card. Number columns "05", "06", "07", "08", "10" under "OCTOBER 2026 · ILLUSTRATIVE REVIEW". Calendar rows contain a finely crafted flat PA-07 ticket spanning05–07, an amber labelled hold at08 and a target line at10. Key specimen clearly "Stoneway Mechanical / PA-07"; large $84,000 requested / $78,000 supported / $6,000 variance. Within timeline: "05 Oct · Review opened", "Waiver missing", "08 Oct · COI expires", "10 Oct · Intended review". Current state reviewer Mara Ellis, GC approval pending. No future events falsely marked done. Every specimen says "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA". Line "No signing or payment execution." 
At below-fold transition an oversized "A date is not a decision." on left and elegant horizontal short real-looking evidence excerpt on right, source labels "SOV-07 v3 / 30 Sep", "CO-03 v1 / 28 Sep", "Lower-tier waiver / Missing". Show a meaningful active-review highlight, not a dense table of features. Realistic small controls and exact data. Main scenario Bridgepine Builders BP-04, September2026 cycle; current actual date15Oct2026, all visual calendar dates are fixed fictional scenario replay, do not call5Oct today.
Bottom discreet art direction footer on same chalk background: "Cycle Study" and three small storyboard vignettes "Documents arrive" / "The hold appears" / "A reviewer takes over", a few color swatches. Motion notes "Calendar compresses into a review timeline on scroll. Native scrolling. Static reduced-motion view." This is ONE concept, not multiple options.
No invented savings, customers, product availability, insurer assurances, fake integrations or legal claims. Only exact supplied marketing copy. Large screen should feel light, fresh, editorial and precise, memorable typographic website with a narrative timeline rather than another dashboard. Avoid repetitive boxes, icons as decoration, shadows, grain, cliché AI art.
prompts.measured:

Soft directional shadows only on dimensional object. No serif, manila, folders, redline, stamps, engineering annotations, gallery exhibits, AI gradients, orb, stock construction photos or generic bento cards.

Header custom DrawPacket simple offset-slab logo and wordmark, Offerings / Workflow / Controls, black "Explore demo" button. "RESEARCH-STAGE CONCEPT" clearly displayed. Wide centered headline EXACT "The difference deserves\na closer look." with small concise subline "Review the amount requested, the evidence behind it and the decision still needed." CTA "Explore synthetic demo" next to "Discuss a pilot".
Hero lower area: oversized BEAUTIFULLY RENDERED SCULPTURAL BAR oriented horizontally like a machined architectural section, subtle axonometric depth but labels face-on. 84 equal units total: 78-unit continuous off-white concrete body supported by evidence and a narrow6-unit persimmon block displaced upward/right, small visible gap. One long supporting line made of 65/5/8 proportionate subtly tinted zones labelled "Current work $65,000", "Stored materials $5,000", "Approved CO $8,000". No more than these data marks. Integrated active record at bottom of hero: "Stoneway Mechanical · PA-07 / Bridgepine Builders · BP-04" and clear "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA". Tiny label "Current-period gross · Illustrative comparison".
Start-of-second-chapter: background becomes pale apricot, far left large "What is still missing?" in black, far right an elegant two-item review list no enclosing cards: warning icon "Lower-tier conditional waiver missing"; warning icon "COI expires before review date". Below divider "Mara Ellis · Reviewer" and "GC approval pending". Statement "No signing or payment execution". Add one small original evidence snippet with source "SOV-07 v3 · 30 Sep 2026" and "CO-03 v1 · 28 Sep 2026", legible.
Current actual date15Oct2026. Fictional fixed demo review5Oct2026, COI expiry8Oct and intended review10Oct; do not label scenario live/today. No real customers/brands, no claimed savings or product efficacy. No fake fully approved results.
Small bottom caption "Measured Difference / Make the exception visible" plus four palette chips, typography specimen and three small motion storyframes "Request" / "Separate the variance" / "Inspect the evidence". Motion concept: bar separates into supported amount and unexplained remainder on scroll; sources attach; no number counters, native scroll and reduced-motion final state.
